newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanians again protest over failed schemes.
newsitem.headline: Albanians again protest over failed schemes.

text.p: Angry Albanian protesters kept up noisy anti-government demonstrations in several southern towns on Friday, with sporadic violence keeping tensions high in the crisis-hit Balkan country.
A teenager was stabbed during the 10th day of protests in the seaside town of Vlore, 150 km (85 miles) south of Tirana. Three people were killed during clashes in Vlore earlier this week.
Witnesses said Adnan Gjoni, 17, was stabbed in the neck and shoulder after accusing a man of being a secret policeman. He was in hospital but out of danger.
A skirmish broke out in Fier, also south of Tirana, when 100 riot police tried to keep several thousand protesters from the central square and town hall, which was burned during clashes last month.

The protesters, enraged after men in civilian clothes attacked a demonstration on Thursday, threw a dozen stones at police trying to push them back from the square. The police quickly gave ground, leaving an uneasy calm.
About 5,000 people demonstrated in Fier and 7,000 in Vlore. Both groups chanted: "Down with (President Sali) Berisha", "We want our money back" and "Thieves, thieves".
Albania, Europe's poorest country, has been swept for the past month by protests and riots by investors who lost their life savings in failed high-risk investment schemes.
The schemes lured new money with offers of high interest rates and then used the cash to pay earlier investors. A large proportion of Albania's adults seem to have joined the schemes.
Investors now blame Berisha's ruling Democratic Party for letting the schemes flourish and opposition parties accuse him of using the schemes to fund his election cam paign last year.

The government, in turn, says opposition groups are trying to exploit the crisis. It impounded about $300 million from two failed funds but steadfastly refused to use government money to reimburse luckless investors.
The main opposition Forum for Democracy snubbed Tritan Shehu, Democratic Party chairman and deputy prime minister, on Friday by refusing to attend all-party talks to discuss the crisis.
Five smaller right-wing parties attended and demanded the resignation of Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi's government.

"The only concrete solution is the resignation of the government which the people no longer believe in," said Hysen Selfo, leader of the National Front Party which has three seats in the 140-member parliament.
"We want the government's resignation because it showed it could not possibly cope with the current situation," said Vasil Melo of the ethnic-Greek Union for Human Rights, which also has three seats.
Meksi's government appears determined to weather the protests and violence but diplomats say the scale of the crisis could be enormous.
Some estimates put the losses from the collapsed schemes at $2 billion, about the size of Albania's annual gross domestic product. Five national schemes have now gone officially bust.
Four more companies, which deny they are pyramids and say they are corporate holdings, have drastically cut back their interest payments and have frozen depositors' assets.
